## Motivation

Valen-2B currently requires its custom Transformers implementation for decision inference. This adds native SGLang loading and `/v1/systemone` serving for `ValenQwenForDecisionMaking` checkpoints, with all questions sharing one causal Qwen3.5 prefill and the trained FP32 Mixer head scoring their candidates.

## Modifications

- Register the Valen config and reuse the native Qwen3.5 backbone, preserving the checkpoint's compute dtype and FP32 decision-head weights. Native serving does not require `--trust-remote-code`.
- Compile Valen's trained prompt format and role spans, preserve candidate order, and pool context/instruction/candidate/decision features across batched requests.
- Support text, conversation states, and images with the checkpoint's resize limits through `/v1/systemone`, including choice, noul, and score questions.
- Enforce complete-prefill execution without prefix reuse, truncation, chunked prefill, or CUDA graphs. This implementation supports shared-state Mixer checkpoints at TP=1/PP=1; video/audio content blocks are explicitly rejected.
- Add compiler, head, config, and serving tests, an end-to-end reference comparison script, and usage documentation.

## Accuracy Tests

- Related CPU regression tests: **54 passed, 1 skipped, 128 subtests passed**.
- Prompt token IDs and role spans matched the published checkpoint implementation for text and image inputs; the FP32 head matched with identical weights/features.
- Real Valen-2B weights on one NVIDIA H200: five reference cases plus 20 mixed requests at concurrency 4. Input token counts and choice results matched. Maximum absolute probability difference from Transformers: **0.00767321**. Maximum concurrent-versus-sequential difference: **0.00742241**. The test's tolerance is 0.02.
- Both default overlap scheduling and `--disable-overlap-schedule` passed the same GPU checks.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed after applying the repository's isort formatting.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/systemone/test_valen.py \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/systemone/test_joint_schema.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/test_joint_schema_head.py \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_decisions.py

python test/manual/valen_reference.py \
  --model-path /models/Valen-2B --output-dir /tmp/valen-check
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One H200, PyTorch 2.14.1/CUDA 13, Transformers 5.19.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, FA3, BF16 backbone compute, FP32 head, and default overlap scheduling. The reference retains the checkpoint's FP32 weights and uses its configured BF16 backbone autocast. Optional Transformers `causal_conv1d` and `flash-linear-attention` kernels were not installed.

These are synthetic smoke benchmarks, with the median of three warmed runs per case. Native timings include local HTTP overhead. They are not a general model-performance claim.

| Case | Input tokens | Transformers (ms) | SGLang (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Short text, three questions | 160 | 39.80 | 27.61 | 1.44× |
| Conversation, three questions | 176 | 38.57 | 27.19 | 1.42× |
| 11-level score | 83 | 35.12 | 26.56 | 1.32× |
| Long text, three questions | 1480 | 97.66 | 30.39 | 3.21× |
| Image, two questions | 312 | 58.45 | 46.82 | 1.25× |

The mixed 20-request run at concurrency 4 achieved **33.15 requests/s**. The script saves raw responses, server logs, launch arguments, per-case latency, and probability differences for inspection.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the repository's pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests and register them in CPU CI.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

+  --model-path Valen-Team/Valen-2B \
+  --tp-size 1 --pp-size 1 \
+  --context-length 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
+```

+Native loading does not require `--trust-remote-code`. The server selects the checkpoint's backbone compute dtype and preserves the head in FP32. +```python Example
+import requests
+
+response = requests.post(
+    "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/systemone",
+    json={
+        "model": "Valen-Team/Valen-2B",
+        "state": "I was charged twice. Please refund the duplicate payment.",
+        "questions": {
+            "team": {
+                "type": "choice",
+                "instructions": "Which team should handle this request?",
+                "criteria": {"billing": "Payments and refunds", "support": "Technical support"},
+            },
+            "urgent": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does this require emergency assistance?"},
+        },
+    },
+    timeout=60,
+)
+response.raise_for_status()
+print(response.json()["answers"])

Prompts are never truncated: their expanded length must fit both `valen_max_length` and the server's prefill limits.

+```json

+  "messages": [
+    {
+      "role": "user",
+      "content": [

+        {"type": "text", "text": "Use this image to answer the questions."}

+    }

+}

+    ("false", "False / 否：不满足问题中的条件。"),
+]

+            )

+    if not 2 <= len(question.criteria) <= 255:
+        raise ValueError("Valen score questions require 2 to 255 levels")

+def _text(value, tokenizer, *, allow_empty=False):
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or (not allow_empty and not value.strip()):
+        raise ValueError("Valen instructions and criteria must be nonempty strings")
+    special = set(tokenizer.all_special_tokens)
+    special.update(
+        str(token) for token in tokenizer.added_tokens_decoder.values() if token.special
+    )
+    if any(token in value for token in special):
+        raise ValueError("Reserved tokenizer control token in Valen input")

+def valen_messages(request, tokenizer):
+    """Render native message state and collect images in placeholder order."""
+    if isinstance(request.state, str):
+        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": request.state}]
+    elif isinstance(request.state, dict) and set(request.state) == {"messages"}:
+        messages = deepcopy(request.state["messages"])
+    else:
+        raise ValueError("Valen state must be text or an object containing messages")
+    if not isinstance(messages, list) or not messages:
+        raise ValueError("Valen state.messages must be a nonempty list")
+    images = []
+    for message in messages:
+        if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") not in {
+            "user",
+            "assistant",
+            "system",
+        }:
+            raise ValueError("Unsupported Valen state message role")
+        content = message.get("content")
+        if isinstance(content, str):
+            content = [{"type": "text", "text": content}]
+        if not isinstance(content, list) or not content:
+            raise ValueError("Valen message content must be text or content blocks")

+            if not isinstance(item, dict):
+                raise ValueError("Invalid Valen content block")
+            if item.get("type") == "text":
+                normalized.append(

+                        "text": _text(item.get("text"), tokenizer, allow_empty=True),
+                    }
+                )

+                if not isinstance(source, dict) or not isinstance(

+                )

+            else:

+                )

+            raise ValueError(
+                "Use image_url blocks for images in a Valen messages state"
+            )

+            ImageData(url=i.url, detail=i.detail or "auto") for i in request.images
+        )

+def encode_valen(tokenizer, request, messages, *, max_length, image_token_counts):
+    # Tokenizing only the template leaves one placeholder per image. The native
+    # multimodal processor expands them later, and the layout shifts accordingly.
+    ids = list(
+        tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+            messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=False, return_dict=False
+        )
+    )

+            if a < span[1] and b > span[0]

+            raise ValueError("Empty token span for Valen decision role")

+    questions = []
+    for i, question in enumerate(request.questions.values()):
+        instruction = _text(question.instructions, tokenizer)
+        prefix = f"Question {i + 1}\nTask: {question.type}\nQuestion: "
+        instruction_span = append(
+            prefix + instruction + "\nCandidates:\n",
+            (len(prefix), len(prefix) + len(instruction)),
+        )
+        spans = []
+        for key, description in valen_options(question):
+            _text(key, tokenizer)
+            _text(description, tokenizer)

+            spans.append(

+                )
+            )

+    for i, (instruction, candidates) in enumerate(questions):
+        append(f"Question {i + 1} Decision:")
+        layout_questions.append(ValenQuestion(instruction, candidates, len(ids) - 1))
+        append("\n")

+    if length > max_length:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Valen prompt has {length} tokens, exceeding max_length={max_length}; no truncation"
+        )
+    return ids, pack_valen_layout(len(ids), context_end, layout_questions)

+"""Valen's FP32 role mixer and packed per-request span layout.
+
+Each candidate reads context, instruction, candidate and decision roles. The
+backbone runs once for all questions; the head batches candidates across requests.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Sequence
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.pooler import EmbeddingPoolerOutput
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ValenQuestion:
+    instruction: tuple[int, int]
+    candidates: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]
+    decision: int
+
+
+def pack_valen_layout(length: int, context_end: int, questions) -> list[int]:
+    """Pack pre-expansion positions into the request's integer layout.
+
+    Header: prompt length, context end, question count. Each question stores
+    instruction start/end, decision position, candidate count, then span pairs.
+    """
+    layout = [length, context_end, len(questions)]
+    for q in questions:
+        layout.extend((*q.instruction, q.decision, len(q.candidates)))
+        for span in q.candidates:
+            layout.extend(span)
+    return layout
+
+
+def parse_valen_layout(layout: Sequence[int], length: int):
+    """Validate a layout and place its roles after image placeholder expansion."""
+    if len(layout) < 3 or any(type(v) is not int for v in layout):
+        raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout must contain integers")
+    original, context, count = layout[:3]
+    shift = length - original
+    if not 0 < context < original or shift < 0 or count < 1:
+        raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout does not match the prompt")
+    cursor, questions = 3, []
+    for _ in range(count):
+        if cursor + 4 > len(layout):
+            raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout is truncated")
+        start, end, decision, n = layout[cursor : cursor + 4]
+        cursor += 4
+        if not context <= start < end <= decision < original or not 1 <= n <= 255:
+            raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout has an invalid question")
+        spans = []
+        for _ in range(n):
+            if cursor + 2 > len(layout):
+                raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout is truncated")
+            a, b = layout[cursor : cursor + 2]
+            cursor += 2
+            if not end <= a < b <= decision:
+                raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout has an invalid candidate")
+            spans.append((a + shift, b + shift))
+        questions.append(
+            ValenQuestion((start + shift, end + shift), tuple(spans), decision + shift)
+        )
+    if cursor != len(layout):
+        raise ValueError("Valen decision_layout has trailing values")
+    # Media expands inside the context, not before its first token.
+    return context + shift, questions
+
+
+class MixerBlock(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, width, token_hidden, channel_hidden):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.token_norm = nn.LayerNorm(width, dtype=torch.float32)
+        self.token_mlp = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(4, token_hidden, dtype=torch.float32),
+            nn.GELU(),
+            nn.Linear(token_hidden, 4, dtype=torch.float32),
+        )
+        self.channel_norm = nn.LayerNorm(width, dtype=torch.float32)
+        self.channel_mlp = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.Linear(width, channel_hidden, dtype=torch.float32),
+            nn.GELU(),
+            nn.Linear(channel_hidden, width, dtype=torch.float32),
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        x = x + self.token_mlp(self.token_norm(x).transpose(1, 2)).transpose(1, 2)
+        return x + self.channel_mlp(self.channel_norm(x))
+
+
+class ValenMixerHead(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, hidden_size, config):
+        super().__init__()
+        defaults = dict(
+            head_width=256,
+            head_layers=2,
+            head_token_hidden_dim=16,
+            head_channel_hidden_dim=1024,
+        )
+        settings = {k: config.get(k, v) for k, v in defaults.items()}
+        if config.get("head_type", "mixer") != "mixer" or any(
+            type(v) is not int or v <= 0 for v in settings.values()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Valen requires a mixer head with positive integer dimensions"
+            )
+        width = settings["head_width"]
+        self.input_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size, dtype=torch.float32)
+        self.projection = nn.Linear(hidden_size, width, dtype=torch.float32)
+        self.roles = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, 4, width, dtype=torch.float32))
+        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(
+            *[
+                MixerBlock(
+                    width,
+                    settings["head_token_hidden_dim"],
+                    settings["head_channel_hidden_dim"],
+                )
+                for _ in range(settings["head_layers"])
+            ]
+        )
+        self.output = nn.Sequential(
+            nn.LayerNorm(width, dtype=torch.float32),
+            nn.Linear(width, 1, dtype=torch.float32),
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, features):
+        x = self.projection(self.input_norm(features.float())) + self.roles
+        return self.output(self.blocks(x)[:, 2]).squeeze(-1)
+
+
+class ValenPooler(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, head):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.head = head
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, forward_batch):
+        outputs = [
+            hidden_states.new_empty(0, dtype=torch.float32)
+            for _ in range(forward_batch.batch_size)
+        ]
+        if (
+            forward_batch.decision_layouts is None
+            or forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu is None
+        ):
+            return EmbeddingPoolerOutput(embeddings=outputs)
+        lengths = forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu
+        prefixes = forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens_cpu or [0] * len(lengths)
+        features, owners, counts = [], [], []
+        offset = 0
+        for i, (layout, length, prefix) in enumerate(
+            zip(forward_batch.decision_layouts, lengths, prefixes)
+        ):
+            hidden = hidden_states[offset : offset + length]
+            offset += length
+            if layout is None:  # Health probe.
+                continue
+            if prefix:
+                continue
+            try:
+                context_end, questions = parse_valen_layout(layout, length)
+            except ValueError:
+                continue
+            context = hidden[:context_end].float().mean(0)
+            count = 0
+            for q in questions:
+                instruction = (
+                    hidden[q.instruction[0] : q.instruction[1]].float().mean(0)
+                )
+                decision = hidden[q.decision].float()
+                for a, b in q.candidates:
+                    features.append(
+                        torch.stack(
+                            (
+                                context,
+                                instruction,
+                                hidden[a:b].float().mean(0),
+                                decision,
+                            )
+                        )
+                    )
+                    count += 1
+            owners.append(i)
+            counts.append(count)
+        if features:
+            logits = self.head(torch.stack(features))
+            for owner, values in zip(owners, logits.split(counts)):
+                outputs[owner] = values
+        return EmbeddingPoolerOutput(embeddings=outputs)

+        command, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True
+    )
+
+    def score(request):
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        response = http.post(
+            url + "/v1/systemone", json={"model": "valen", **request}, timeout=180
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        return response.json(), time.perf_counter() - start
+
+    try:
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 600
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            if server.poll() is not None:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"Server exited with {server.returncode}; see server.log"
+                )
+            try:
+                response = http.get(url + "/health", timeout=2)
+                if response.status_code == 200:
+                    break
+            except http.RequestException:
+                pass
+            time.sleep(2)
+        else:
+            raise TimeoutError("SGLang did not become ready within 600 seconds")
+        answers, timings = [], []
+        for request in requests:
+            score(request)
+            runs = [score(request) for _ in range(args.repeats)]
+            answers.append(runs[-1][0])
+            timings.append(statistics.median(t for _, t in runs))
+        concurrent_requests = [
+            copy.deepcopy(requests[i % len(requests)]) for i in range(20)
+        ]
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
+            batch = list(pool.map(score, concurrent_requests))
+        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+        result = {
+            "answers": answers,
+            "median_seconds": timings,
+            "concurrent_answers": [a for a, _ in batch],
+            "concurrent_seconds": elapsed,
+            "concurrent_requests_per_second": len(batch) / elapsed,
+        }
+        (args.output_dir / "native.json").write_text(
+            json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+        )
+    finally:
+        import signal
+
+        os.killpg(server.pid, signal.SIGTERM) if server.poll() is None else None
+        try:
+            server.wait(timeout=30)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            os.killpg(server.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            server.wait()
+        log.close()
+
+
+def compare(args):
+    reference = json.loads((args.output_dir / "reference.json").read_text())
+    native = json.loads((args.output_dir / "native.json").read_text())
+    if len(reference["answers"]) != 5 or len(native["answers"]) != 5:
+        raise ValueError("Expected all five parity cases")
+    if len(native["concurrent_answers"]) != 20:
+        raise ValueError("Expected all twenty concurrent responses")
+    rows = []
+    max_error = 0.0
+    tokens_match = True
+    choices_match = True
+    for i, (expected, actual) in enumerate(
+        zip(reference["answers"], native["answers"])
+    ):
+        tokens_match &= (
+            expected["usage"]["input_tokens"] == actual["usage"]["input_tokens"]
+        )
+        if expected["answers"].keys() != actual["answers"].keys():
+            raise ValueError("Native response question keys differ from reference")
+        error = 0.0
+        for key, answer in expected["answers"].items():
+            got = actual["answers"][key]
+            if answer["type"] != got["type"]:
+                raise ValueError("Native response answer type differs from reference")
+            values = (
+                [got["noul"]]
+                if got["type"] == "noul"
+                else list(got["probabilities"].values())
+            )
+            if not all(math.isfinite(value) for value in values):
+                raise ValueError("Non-finite native probability")
+            if answer["type"] == "noul":
+                error = max(error, abs(answer["noul"] - got["noul"]))
+            else:
+                error = max(
+                    error,
+                    *(
+                        abs(p - got["probabilities"][k])
+                        for k, p in answer["probabilities"].items()
+                    ),
+                )
+            if answer["type"] == "choice":
+                choices_match &= answer["choice"] == got["choice"]
+        max_error = max(error, max_error)
+        rows.append(
+            {
+                "case": i,
+                "prompt_tokens": expected["usage"]["input_tokens"],
+                "max_probability_error": error,
+                "reference_seconds": reference["median_seconds"][i],
+                "native_seconds": native["median_seconds"][i],
+                "speedup": reference["median_seconds"][i] / native["median_seconds"][i],
+            }
+        )
+    batch_error = 0.0
+    for i, answer in enumerate(native["concurrent_answers"]):
+        expected = native["answers"][i % len(rows)]
+        for key, got in answer["answers"].items():
+            ref = expected["answers"][key]
+            values = (
+                [abs(got["noul"] - ref["noul"])]
+                if got["type"] == "noul"
+                else [
+                    abs(p - ref["probabilities"][k])
+                    for k, p in got["probabilities"].items()
+                ]
+            )
+            batch_error = max(batch_error, *values)
+    result = {
+        "cases": rows,
+        "tokens_match": tokens_match,
+        "choices_match": choices_match,
+        "max_probability_error": max_error,
+        "batch_max_probability_error": batch_error,
+        "concurrent_requests_per_second": native["concurrent_requests_per_second"],
+        "tolerance": args.tolerance,
+        "passed": tokens_match
+        and choices_match
+        and max(max_error, batch_error) <= args.tolerance,
+    }
+    (args.output_dir / "comparison.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
+    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2), flush=True)
+    if not result["passed"]:
+        raise SystemExit("Valen parity check failed")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--model-path", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--mode", choices=["all", "reference", "native", "compare"], default="all"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=31000)
+    parser.add_argument("--tolerance", type=float, default=0.02)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    args.output_dir = args.output_dir.resolve()
+    args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    requests = cases(args.output_dir)
+    if args.mode == "all":
+        for mode in ("reference", "native", "compare"):
+            subprocess.run(
+                [
+                    sys.executable,
+                    __file__,
+                    "--model-path",
+                    args.model_path,
+                    "--output-dir",
+                    str(args.output_dir),
+                    "--mode",
+                    mode,
+                    "--repeats",
+                    str(args.repeats),
+                    "--port",
+                    str(args.port),
+                    "--tolerance",
+                    str(args.tolerance),
+                ],
+                check=True,
+            )
+    elif args.mode == "reference":
+        reference(args, requests)
+    elif args.mode == "native":
+        native(args, requests)
+    else:
+        compare(args)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
